spec_match.rationale: Demonstrates the spec's ::column special case — markers derived from column fragments with tabs mode routing the tabpanel role to the fragments' originating element — using the real ::column::scroll-marker selectors and scroll-marker-group: after tabs.

interactive.rationale: Type-size and column-width sliders re-fragment the article live, the derived dot count changes with them, the pager dots navigate, and a measured page-count readout updates on scroll and resize.

blurb_alignment.rationale: The index promises a multi-column article whose pager re-derives itself when type grows; the sliders do exactly that.

edge_cases.rationale: Covers re-pagination and the no-column fallback tiers, but not writing-mode/vertical fragmentation or what happens to the active tab when the current page disappears during re-fragmentation.

references.rationale: chromestatus entry, the modes section and the ::column pseudo-element section are all linked.

conformance.rationale: Grammar tiers used here are pinned in the feature suite; the role-routing sentence is covered by the manual assertion since no scriptable probe can observe it.

runtime_evidence.rationale: Headless Chromium 141: dots render one-per-column, autorun grew type from 1.0rem to 1.5rem and the measured page count changed with the assert passing (4 pages at 672px viewport), console clean, mobile emulation overflow-free. The tabs-mode role routing itself cannot be observed on 141 and is bannered as such.

telemetry_health.rationale: Asserts the capability probe, the fallback branch and the autorun re-pagination result with before/after page counts.

design_system.rationale: Variables only; the derived dots use bordered paper/black states with AA contrast; the marker group has an explicit height so the contain:size box reserves real space.

accessibility.rationale: Sliders are labelled with live value text, the reader region has an aria-label and the page count is aria-live — but the derived dots use content:"" and so carry no accessible name on pre-modes browsers; what name tabs mode gives fragment-derived tabs is an open question below.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: CDP-emulated 360x740 DPR3: zero horizontal overflow (the reader scrolls internally by design), controls stack, no console errors.

guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Use intrinsic sizing and container-relative units so components re-derive their layout instead of hard-coding breakpoints.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: The whole demo is that principle applied to pagination: the column count and pager derive from available space and font size, and the controls simply vary those inputs.

guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Reflect the actively snapped item visually.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: :target-current fills the active page's derived dot; the measured readout gives the textual equivalent.

openQuestions.title: Determine the accessible name of fragment-derived tab markers
openQuestions.detail: The dots are content:"" markers over ::column fragments, so on pre-modes browsers they expose no accessible name. Verify on a Chrome 154 build what tabs mode announces for fragment-derived tabs (position-in-set only?), and if it is silent, add counter(scroll-marker-like) content or generated text so each dot announces 'page N'.

openQuestions.title: Active-page behaviour when re-fragmentation removes the current page
openQuestions.detail: Shrink type while on the last page: does the browser keep a dangling active marker, snap to the new last page, or reset to page 1? Journal this on a modes-enabled build and document the observed behaviour on the page.

summary: Advanced composition: multicol fragmentation + derived scroll markers + tabs mode as a self-deriving paged reader, with honest geometry-based page measurement. Verified headless on Chromium 141 (dots track re-pagination, autorun assert passed, clean console, mobile clean); role routing and dot naming on a real 154 build are the recorded open questions.
